Ammonia Plants

Key points covered

  • Corporate NDT cohorts for ammonia synthesis loops, primary and secondary reformers, urea reactors, and high-pressure synthesis-gas piping. Built around ASME Section VIII Div 2, ASME B31.3 process piping, NACE MR0103 for sour service, and the specific reformer-tube creep-inspection toolkit (LOTIS, eddy current, replication) that defines modern ammonia plant integrity programs.
  • Ultrasonic Testing — PAUT for synthesis-loop converters + TOFD for thick-wall vessels
  • Ammonia converter inspectors, urea reactor QC, syngas heat-exchanger integrity teams
  • Radiographic Testing — Ir-192 + Se-75 for syngas + ammonia piping welds
  • Magnetic Particle Testing — WFMT + AC yoke for sour-service stress-corrosion
  • Hardness testing + chemical replication for HTHA + sulfide-stress surveillance
  • Reformer-tube inspectors trained on LOTIS only, without the replication + hardness backup discipline that defines the modern ammonia plant integrity program
  • Tubes flagged for replacement that have remaining life; or worse, tubes accepted that fail in the next campaign — unplanned outage measured in millions per day.
  • Pressure-vessel inspectors fluent in API 510 but unfamiliar with API 579 fitness-for-service for creep + HTHA damage
  • FFS decisions outsourced unnecessarily to specialist consultants at $100K+ per assessment; or accept/reject calls made on rule-of-thumb without code defence.
  • Welding inspectors holding AWS CWI without NACE MR0103 sulfide-stress-cracking awareness on sour-service welds
  • Heat-affected zone hardness exceedances on sour-service welds; rework cost in the hundreds of thousands per spread on capital projects.
  • PAUT operators trained on hydrocarbon vessels who cannot defend scan plans on ammonia synthesis converter targets (sub-surface HTHA, hydrogen attack)
  • Audit findings during commissioning by Yara, CF Industries, QAFCO, IFFCO — scan rejected, vessel re-inspected, ammonia plant restart delayed.
  • Recurrent training cadence set at 5-year default rather than the 3-year cadence typical at ammonia offtaker audits
  • Insurer surveys and operator pre-turnaround audits flag stale qualification records — turnaround critical path delayed.
  • Level II UT + MT + replication + hardness, then API RP 573 + API RP 941 module
  • Level II UT + RT + MT, then API 570 inspector + API 1104 pipeline module
  • Multi-asset annual contract; reformer-specific written-practice bridging included.
  • Ammonia plant cohorts are dominated by hybrid delivery, with reformer-integrity practicals running as a separate on-site workshop during planned outages. Theory on the LMS during the build-up to a turnaround; practicals on-site in the 2–4 weeks before shutdown; reformer LOTIS / ECT / replication workshops scheduled to coincide with reformer tube-pull events. AWS D1.1 + B31.3 + ASME VIII inspection is delivered on the operator's own coupons and weld test plates so essential-variable transfer is genuine.
  • Ammonia plant audits (Yara, CF Industries, QAFCO, IFFCO, Nutrien, OCI Nitrogen) all run to slightly different layouts but ask for the same underlying evidence — SNT-TC-1A written practice references, training hours mapped to Recommended Hours Table 6.3, exam grade sheets retained five years, vision and OJT logs signed by the supervising Level II or III, and the reformer-specific written practice for LOTIS / ECT / replication competence. Our delivery captures all of that automatically and exports it in the layout your operator and lender's engineer expect.
  • Major ammonia / urea operator — Middle East — 42-engineer multi-method cohort, 12-week programme
